cases.classification: Requested jump did not produce confirmed takeoff
findings: All three jump requests were punctual, each less than 4 ms after its schedule. Each received the existing retry; none produced confirmed upward movement.

The body was parked with zero requested movement. An approaching opponent closed from 4.17 to 1.37 studs before the first request; the root was then displaced horizontally while still commanding zero movement.
During held Jump, the native state reported Jumping but root height fell below its prior standing height and vertical velocity remained nonpositive.
Later planner snapshots still used the actual positive jump speed of 48.522 studs/s and reported the jump state enabled through canJump=true.
No native contact-effect event was captured for this interval.
cases.assessment: Physical interference during the parked takeoff is the strongest observed explanation, but client telemetry does not prove the exact native reason the jump produced no lift. This is distinct from a valid local claim rejected by authoritative catch arbitration.
cases.response: Add passive properties/state/body-gap fields to existing jumpRequest and jumpRetry events. Do not force native airborne state, modify jump properties or increase retry frequency.
limitations: The exact Humanoid JumpHeight/JumpPower/state-enabled values at dispatch and retry are not separately recorded.
Opponent replication and body collision responses are not reconstructed by offline ballistic replay.
Proximity alone is not proof of jump suppression; successful near-body catches are retained as controls.

cases.classification: Fresh local diving contact was not awarded possession; pursuit could not close the recovery gap

pursuit.interpretation: The initial dive recovered well behind the carrier; ordinary sprint pursuit never reached tackle range before the touchdown.

findings: Jump and dive were both dispatched within the existing action budgets, and a fresh airborne local contact was recorded.
The reported network-ping metric was about 160 ms, higher than the earlier reviewed contested contacts. The result was observed 818 ms after the local claim.
Longer callback gaps were captured before this throw; the actual jump and dive dispatches remained punctual.
cases.geometricInferenceOnly: The result position projection is a spatial trajectory comparison, not authoritative catch timing or server receipt order.
cases.response: Retain the loss and full postcatch pursuit in evaluation. Do not force claims, extend dive reach, change speed or assume higher latency proves the rejection cause.

earlierContactSearch.sampling: First observed native-sprint and last grounded snapshots for each loss; explicit bounded time/action grids, not a proof over every possible control.
earlierContactSearch.constraints: Existing 0.4 margin,12 ms contact half-window,60 ms jump and20 ms dive timing variants, connected first contact for dives, field bounds, observed stamina/speed and no intermediate airborne stopping.
earlierContactSearch.conclusion: No earlier ordinary dive was omitted in this bounded search. A new grounded launch-point stop or a changed upright stopping target offers roughly 6–7ms of modeled first-contact gain; finer jump timing alone offers 1–2ms. These unintegrated alternatives do not establish why the server awarded the losses or that the outcomes would reverse.

nativeInputReview: The controller computes jump speed from current Humanoid JumpHeight or JumpPower; it does not replace zero with a configuration default.
The request remains held during the pending interval; the sampled jumpHeld=true agrees with that behavior.
The existing stale-action deadline cancels each request approximately 80 ms after its schedule. It does not prematurely confirm takeoff or permit a dive through the native floor guard.

The inspected native team jump limiter would zero JumpHeight; the later positive jump-speed snapshots do not match a sustained limiter activation. A transient property change at the exact request is not observable from existing logs.

checks: Post-input native jump-height change is recorded without altering dispatch.
Missing body/floor details do not suppress input.
Throwing native-property reads retain the action and partial event.
Retry and event counts remain unchanged.

limits: This is an incident audit, not proof of perfect play or a controlled win-rate improvement.
Local contact geometry does not guarantee authoritative possession.
Native body interaction and unknown authoritative catch arbitration are not reproduced by the offline solver.
The small alternative first-touch gains have not been validated in native execution; no planner ranking or catch-buffer change was made from this search.
The missed-takeoff response in this release is diagnostic only. Its exact native cause remains unproven.
